newsitem.title: USA: Top U.S. officer says Iraq tries to hide missiles.
newsitem.headline: Top U.S. officer says Iraq tries to hide missiles.

text.p: Iraqi forces have been shuffling antiaircraft defenses in the southern "no fly" zone in Iraq in an effort to hide them, the top U.S. military officer charged on Sunday.

"We see the missile sights still there," General John Shalikashvili, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, said on the ABC progam "This Week with David Brinkley". "We see a moving around, trying to hide them from us," he said.

Shalikashvili said the United States had not seen any Iraqi effort in the "last few days" to defy the United States by reconstructing missile sites disabled by cruise missile strikes earlier this month.

U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher, appearing on the CBS programme "Face the Nation," said he expected Kuwait to give the go-ahead for the United States to send in up to 5,000 more Army troops as part of the U.S. buildup in the area.
"The president has authorised the moving of those troops and I suspect they will move in due course," Christopher said.
Shalikashvili, for his part, said, "it's my expectation that we will hear very shortly that they (Kuwait) will be delighted to accept those troops."
"What we are seeing on the ground is sort of a mixed story," Shalikashvili said. "The intelligence is in fact mixed about what Saddam is doing with his missile sites."
